text:
sarah: Heads up — noticed billing events backlog from penumbra feeder starting ~10:02 UTC. Ingest-to-audit SLO (30s) is failing for ~10% of traffic, latency up to ~120s for affected shards.

mike: Any obvious root cause?

sarah: Two things combined: a large batch from one tenant (spike) + a retry storm from our runtime after an unrelated transient. Queue at ingress spiked and our flush window/compact logic got overwhelmed.

opsbot: :information_source: Incident created INC-2026-321 (penumbra feeder backlog) — paging eng-platform oncall.

julia: Is this the same path that runs the audit enrichment step? If enrichment is the bottleneck we should consider fast-pathing minimal audit markers.

sarah: Yes, enrichment is CPU-heavy; it's the critical path to mark events as auditable. Right now we hold until enrichment completes before emitting the billing event.

arjun: Tradeoffs: we can either (A) buffer longer, (B) shed/drop low-value events, or (C) emit lightweight audit markers and replay enrichment async. Each has implications for billing accuracy and posthoc audits.

nina: For compliance we can't silently drop everything. But we can drop non-billable telemetry or sample. Suggest "value-aware sampling": keep 100% of high-value tenants/events, sample small requests.

mike: Agreed. Also need to preserve idempotency so replay won't double-charge if we emit placeholders now and enriched later. Our event_id + attempt metadata should be the source of truth.

arjun: Proposal: implement a soft-shed shaper at ingress with these rules:
```
shaper:
  mode: soft-shed
  default_sample_rate: 0.05
  high_value_rate: 1.0
  priority_keys: ["tenant_id", "api_key", "request_cost_estimate"]
  buffer_seconds: 60
  emit_placeholder: true
```
Placeholders = lightweight billing events with minimal attribution fields and state="pending_enrich". Enrichment runs async and emits a final audit record that references the placeholder event_id.

julia: Placeholder approach seems good — keeps pipeline moving and preserves an audit chain. Need to ensure downstream billing reconciler can join placeholders with final enriched records.

sarah: We should also add a fallback route: if enrichment backlog > X, route placeholders to cold storage (compressed) and emit only a summarized charge (approx) to avoid huge tail latency. Then replay enrichment from cold storage when load normalizes.

nina: What about correctness of charges? Summarized charge risks undercharging; we need a reconciliation job that compares placeholder approximations vs final enriched charges and issues corrective adjustments. That introduces latency but keeps availability.

mike: Operationally we need metrics: placeholder_rate, placeholder_lag (time until enrichment), replay_queue_size, summary_error_rate, and audit_mismatch_count. Also set an SLO for reconciliation window (e.g., 24h) and alert if past due.

arjun: On idempotency: placeholder and final enriched event MUST share the same canonical event_id. Replay job must be careful to update ledger entries instead of inserting duplicates. Add a flag to the billing write path: upsert_mode: "merge_on_event_id".

julia: Implementation concerns: ledger writes are the expensive hot path. Merging updates increases contention. Consider writing enrichment diffs to an append-only corrections topic, and have a separate reconciler apply corrections in controlled batches to the ledger to reduce write contention.

nina: That matches compliance needs: all corrections are auditable and we keep a compacted origin stream.

mike: What about sampling policy config rollout? We need per-tenant overrides and emergency controls to set sampling rates to 0 or 1 at runtime. Feature flags + console controls.

sarah: Agreed. Also add a cheap heuristic to detect "retry storms" and lower default_sample_rate temporarily to protect the system.

arjun: Risk: sampling alters long-tail billing analytics. We must document the sampling bias and ensure analytics teams know how to reweight sampled data. Provide a sampled_multiplier in emited placeholders so downstream can estimate true counts.

julia: Security/compliance note: placeholders must not leak sensitive prompt/text fields. Keep placeholders minimal. Enriched records in cold storage can be more complete but encrypted with tenant KMS.

mike: Quick checklist of next steps (small actionable items):
1) Implement ingress shaper prototype (soft-shed + placeholder emission) — owner @arjun — due EOD +2
2) Add placeholder schema and upsert semantics for ledger writer — owner @julia — due EOD +3
3) Reconciler design doc for corrections topic and batch applier — owner @nina — due EOD +4
4) Console emergency controls + feature flag for sampling per-tenant — owner @sarah — due EOD +5
5) Instrument placeholder metrics and set alerts — owner @mike — due EOD +2

sarah: I can take the rollout coordination and run a tabletop for the reconciliation flows tomorrow.

opsbot: :white_check_mark: Incident INC-2026-321 acknowledged by eng-platform oncall.

arjun: One more: add a test harness that can simulate a tenant spike + retries so we can validate placeholder->enrich->reconcile correctness before turning on in prod. I'll start a small harness repo.

julia: Sounds good. If we keep placeholder payloads tiny and ensure canonical event_ids, this should buy us availability while preserving auditability.

nina: I'll draft the compliance note about retention/encryption for cold storage.

mike: TL;DR: soft-shed + placeholders + async enrichment + reconciler = availability-first, auditable correctness via later reconciliation.

sarah: Thanks all — capturing AIs in the doc and we'll follow up in the RFC thread later.

mike: :thumbsup:
